correctness.rationale: The claimed estimator is a quadratic-minus-quartic polynomial. At alpha=0 all contributions are nonnegative; for alpha>0 a singular-vector sketch with first columns tv and tu yields sigma²[(1+alpha)t²/r-alpha t⁴/r²]<0 above t²>r(1+alpha)/alpha, giving a positive-probability Gaussian open set for every nonzero matrix. In rank one X,Y are independent chi-square_r/r and negativity means XY>c(X+Y) with c=(1+alpha)/(2alpha). The integral follows by conditioning. The rate function I(x)+I(y) has unique boundary saddle (2c,2c), J(c)=2c-1-log(2c); the local t/r and d/sqrt(r) coordinates produce prefactor 1/[sqrt(2pi r)(2c-1)sqrt(4c-1)]. The c_r=1+2/r perturbation yields the oracle e^-2 factor. We independently expanded the saddle Hessian and Jacobian; no finite check was substituted for the large-r argument.
